text:
tasha: quick sync from the sentinel-stitch experiment. onboarding cedar-liteq. streaming funcall suite shows ~1.9% schema.fail only on streaming; non-streaming clean. hypothesis: chunk boundary ambiguity causing micro-reorders and truncated fields.

omar: can you summarize what you tried already?

tasha: tried sanitizer and ndjson-wrap repairs; helped but we still see clusters under high throughput. so i prototyped a tiny runtime sentinel: emitter appends a short printable marker at safe cut points: `<SPLIT:crc16>` (opt-in). assembler validates CRC and prefers stitching at sentinel boundaries. early results: failure rate drops to 0.12% from 1.9% on small runs.

will: nifty. is the sentinel inserted as raw text between tokens? could that break tokenization for some decoders?

tasha: it's inserted as a separate top-level byte sequence between objects only when runtime determines a safe cut (i.e., between completed top-level JSON objects). runtime change is opt-in per model. not emitted inside strings.

omar: any risk of the sentinel being stripped by proxies or sidecars? we saw earlier that some network layers normalize control bytes. using printable ascii reduces that risk.

telemetry: note: metric sample from dogfood run (5k streams): schema.fail_rate before=1.86%, after=0.12%, sentinel_mismatch_rate=0.04%, avg_tail_latency +3ms when assembler waits for sentinel with max_wait_ms=40.

will: good numbers. how do we handle streams that don't include sentinels (older runtimes)?

tasha: assembler fallback order: 1) if sentinel present, stitch by sentinel CRC (fast path), 2) elif ndjson_wrap enabled, attempt safe wrap/reparse, 3) else run sanitizer/repair attempts. All behind flags.

omar: did you verify downstream tool execution idempotency? sentinel could change timing and produce different side-effect order if we buffer.

tasha: yes — ran divergence check: replayed 10k previously-failed streams with sentinel enabled vs repair-only. tool.exec_divergence=0.007% (within acceptable) and we recorded exec_attempts metric so we can watch duplicates.

will: what about rollout? runtime change + assembler change needs coordination. plan?

tasha: RFC: land assembler support first (flags: --stream-sentinel-enabled, --stream-sentinel-max-wait-ms), dogfood with runtime emitting sentinels in a small canary pool. Runtime will expose opt-in model config `emit_split_sentinel: true` in canary image. If dogfood stable, flip more models.

omar: add metrics: sentinel.used_count, sentinel.mismatch_count, sentinel.wait_time_p90, parse.fallback_repair_count. Also add alert if sentinel_mismatch_rate > 0.5% over 30m.

telemetry: added dashboards: Sentinels -> used_count / mismatch_rate, Streams -> schema.fail_rate by model+quant.

will: tests?

tasha: unit: crc16 generation/verification; integration: runtime + assembler kubernetes dogfood job with deterministic seed: `python tests/sentinel_repro.py --model cedar-liteq --seed 2026 --requests 10000 --emit-sentinel` ; fuzz: random chunking with/without sentinel to assert assembler chooses correct path.

omar: any perf concern? extra bytes and small buffering adds tail but seems minimal. also check cost metric: tiny bump in request CPU due to CRC checks; included in telemetry as parse.cpu_millis.

merge-bot: PR opened: r/5582 sentinel-stitching opt-in (https://git.internal/r/5582). CI green.

will: looks good. let's run dogfood on a small dedicated pool overnight and collect sentinel_mismatch and tool.exec_divergence. If stable, schedule runtime sidecar canary to enable emit_split_sentinel for a handful of models tomorrow.

tasha: will run dogfood and paste metrics here. thanks all. :raised_hands:
